verdict: No mathematical soundness defect found in check() for finite JSON certificates.
findings: The fixed template is SB(phi) implies seed/hull closure plus unrestricted image support.
Template calls reset the matrix-local binder stack and pass only input/output slot values across the call boundary.
Matrix parameter assignments persist through all shared calls.
Every hidden parameter-map value is allocated before use; negative-universal witnesses remain fresh in all active closure environments.
Implication and quantifier rules have the standard classical signed-tableau signs.
Every branch must close on opposite evaluated relation atoms or positive primitive Bottom.
Dynamic AX maps allow schema parameters to use witnesses introduced after the matrix pool was chosen.
Existing positive universals remain available for later gamma instantiations.
soundness_invariant: Before each instruction, every ID in active bound stacks, slot pairs, and root parameter-map values is less than counter.
completeness_obligation: Give the usual finite-tableau translation, including removal of gratuitous gamma constants and dynamic universal-schema instantiation.
scope: This review covers the shared-template certificate checker. It does not establish fairness of an enumerator, internal ZFC formalization, or correctness and state count of a compiled binary blank-tape TM.
minor_issue_at_review: An explicit --theorem file containing JSON null selected the default refutation interface. This could not create a false accepted refutation; parent indicated it would be fixed.
